blocks.text: Śiva Sūtras 3.13
blocks.directed: [long pause] Śiva Sūtras 3.13

blocks.text: सिद्धः स्वतन्त्रभावः
blocks.directed: [slowly] सिद्धः स्वतन्त्रभावः

blocks.text: Siddhaḥ svatantrabhāvaḥ.
blocks.directed: Siddhaḥ svatantrabhāvaḥ.

blocks.text: The state of being free and independent is attained.
blocks.directed: The state of being free and independent is attained.

blocks.text: Svātantrya: The Entire Point of the Bloody Operation.
blocks.directed: Svātantrya: The Entire Point of the Bloody Operation.

blocks.text: Now we’re talking.
blocks.directed: Now we’re talking.

blocks.text: Because this is where everything comes together.
blocks.directed: Because this is where everything comes together.

blocks.text: Siddhaḥ — accomplished, attained, realised.
blocks.directed: Siddhaḥ — accomplished, attained, realised.

blocks.text: Svatantra — independent, self-governing, free.
blocks.directed: Svatantra — independent, self-governing, free.

blocks.text: Bhāvaḥ — state, condition, manner of being.
blocks.directed: Bhāvaḥ — state, condition, manner of being.

blocks.text: And the key word is svatantra.
blocks.directed: And the key word is svatantra.

blocks.text: Let’s look at its construction.
blocks.directed: Let’s look at its construction.

blocks.text: Sva — one’s own, belonging to oneself.
blocks.directed: Sva — one’s own, belonging to oneself.

blocks.text: Tantra — here conveying the principle of control, dependence or governance.
blocks.directed: Tantra — here conveying the principle of control, dependence or governance.

blocks.text: Svatantra therefore means self-dependent, independent, governed by oneself rather than by another.
blocks.directed: Svatantra therefore means self-dependent, independent, governed by oneself rather than by another.

blocks.text: And the abstract noun:
blocks.directed: [short pause] And the abstract noun:

blocks.text: Svātantrya.
blocks.directed: [slowly] Svātantrya.

blocks.text: Freedom.
blocks.directed: Freedom.

blocks.text: Independence.
blocks.directed: Independence.

blocks.text: Autonomy.
blocks.directed: Autonomy.

blocks.text: But in Trika, it becomes something much more radical than ordinary personal autonomy.
blocks.directed: But in Trika, it becomes something much more radical than ordinary personal autonomy.

blocks.text: It is the intrinsic freedom of supreme consciousness.
blocks.directed: It is the intrinsic freedom of supreme consciousness.

blocks.text: The power through which Śiva knows, acts and manifests.
blocks.directed: The power through which Śiva knows, acts and manifests.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja explains that this freedom involves sahajajñatva and kartṛtva.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja explains that this freedom involves sahajajñatva and kartṛtva.

blocks.text: Innate knowledge and agency.
blocks.directed: Innate knowledge and agency.

blocks.text: The natural powers of knowing and acting.
blocks.directed: The natural powers of knowing and acting.

blocks.text: Now think about the limited individual.
blocks.directed: Now think about the limited individual.

blocks.text: The aṇu.
blocks.directed: The aṇu.

blocks.text: Its knowledge is restricted.
blocks.directed: Its knowledge is restricted.

blocks.text: Its agency is restricted.
blocks.directed: Its agency is restricted.

blocks.text: Its experience is structured by time, necessity, desire and differentiated cognition.
blocks.directed: Its experience is structured by time, necessity, desire and differentiated cognition.

blocks.text: And the entire third book began by describing precisely this condition.
blocks.directed: And the entire third book began by describing precisely this condition.

blocks.text: But now the yogi, through the recognition of the subtle reality of consciousness, attains the condition of freedom.
blocks.directed: But now the yogi, through the recognition of the subtle reality of consciousness, attains the condition of freedom.

blocks.text: What’s being reversed?
blocks.directed: What’s being reversed?

blocks.text: The fundamental limitations through which Śiva experienced himself as a finite subject.
blocks.directed: The fundamental limitations through which Śiva experienced himself as a finite subject.

blocks.text: The point isn’t simply:
blocks.directed: [short pause] The point isn’t simply:

blocks.text: “I can now do whatever I want.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I can now do whatever I want.”

blocks.text: That’s ordinary individual desire enlarged into a fantasy.
blocks.directed: That’s ordinary individual desire enlarged into a fantasy.

blocks.text: Nor is it:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Nor is it:

blocks.text: “I am an exceptionally powerful personality who deserves to control everybody else.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I am an exceptionally powerful personality who deserves to control everybody else.”

blocks.text: That would be ahaṃkāra wearing a very expensive Śaiva costume.
blocks.directed: That would be ahaṃkāra wearing a very expensive Śaiva costume.

blocks.text: The claim is that the yogi recognises the nature of consciousness as intrinsically free.
blocks.directed: The claim is that the yogi recognises the nature of consciousness as intrinsically free.

blocks.text: And this freedom isn’t merely freedom from particular external obstacles.
blocks.directed: And this freedom isn’t merely freedom from particular external obstacles.

blocks.text: It’s the freedom through which manifestation itself is understood.
blocks.directed: It’s the freedom through which manifestation itself is understood.

blocks.text: Consider the difference.
blocks.directed: Consider the difference.

blocks.text: Ordinary freedom means:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Ordinary freedom means:

blocks.text: “I have a choice between several possibilities.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I have a choice between several possibilities.”

blocks.text: Divine svātantrya means something more fundamental.
blocks.directed: Divine svātantrya means something more fundamental.

blocks.text: The very existence of manifested possibilities belongs to the freedom of consciousness.
blocks.directed: The very existence of manifested possibilities belongs to the freedom of consciousness.

blocks.text: Śiva doesn’t merely select among pre-existing options arranged by some independent cosmic administrator.
blocks.directed: Śiva doesn’t merely select among pre-existing options arranged by some independent cosmic administrator.

blocks.text: Within the Trika system, the appearance of those options is itself an expression of Śakti.
blocks.directed: Within the Trika system, the appearance of those options is itself an expression of Śakti.

blocks.text: That’s why svātantrya is so central.
blocks.directed: That’s why svātantrya is so central.

blocks.text: It distinguishes Śiva from an inert absolute.
blocks.directed: It distinguishes Śiva from an inert absolute.

blocks.text: Consciousness is not merely luminous.
blocks.directed: Consciousness is not merely luminous.

blocks.text: It is self-aware, active, and endowed with the freedom of manifestation.
blocks.directed: It is self-aware, active, and endowed with the freedom of manifestation.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja explicitly describes the attained freedom as sovereignty involving natural knowledge and agency.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja explicitly describes the attained freedom as sovereignty involving natural knowledge and agency.

blocks.text: He cites a teaching attributed to Nāthapāda identifying the power of freedom with Kālī, the supreme power.
blocks.directed: He cites a teaching attributed to Nāthapāda identifying the power of freedom with Kālī, the supreme power.

blocks.text: And he cites the Svacchandatantra on the yogi’s sovereignty over the tattvas, beings, letters and mantras through contemplation of Śiva. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: And he cites the Svacchandatantra on the yogi’s sovereignty over the tattvas, beings, letters and mantras through contemplation of Śiva. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: Now, the latter includes a traditional claim of extraordinary yogic sovereignty.
blocks.directed: Now, the latter includes a traditional claim of extraordinary yogic sovereignty.

blocks.text: That should not be mistaken for a scientifically established power to control the physical universe.
blocks.directed: That should not be mistaken for a scientifically established power to control the physical universe.

blocks.text: But its philosophical significance is profound.
blocks.directed: But its philosophical significance is profound.

blocks.text: The yogi’s highest freedom is not another limited object of attainment.
blocks.directed: The yogi’s highest freedom is not another limited object of attainment.

blocks.text: It is the recognition of the divine power that makes manifestation possible.
blocks.directed: It is the recognition of the divine power that makes manifestation possible.

blocks.text: And this brings us back to the beginning.
blocks.directed: And this brings us back to the beginning.

blocks.text: चैतन्यमात्मा।
blocks.directed: [slowly] चैतन्यमात्मा।

blocks.text: Consciousness is the Self.
blocks.directed: Consciousness is the Self.

blocks.text: But now that statement has acquired a far richer meaning.
blocks.directed: But now that statement has acquired a far richer meaning.

blocks.text: Consciousness is not merely a container of appearances.
blocks.directed: Consciousness is not merely a container of appearances.

blocks.text: It is not merely an observer.
blocks.directed: It is not merely an observer.

blocks.text: It is the free, self-revealing reality through which appearances become manifest.
blocks.directed: It is the free, self-revealing reality through which appearances become manifest.

blocks.text: Svātantrya is inseparable from what Śiva is.
blocks.directed: Svātantrya is inseparable from what Śiva is.

blocks.text: And liberation is recognition of that nature.
blocks.directed: And liberation is recognition of that nature.

blocks.text: Not the construction of an entirely new Self.
blocks.directed: Not the construction of an entirely new Self.

blocks.text: Not the acquisition of something fundamentally external.
blocks.directed: Not the acquisition of something fundamentally external.

blocks.text: The recognition of one’s own deepest reality.
blocks.directed: The recognition of one’s own deepest reality.

blocks.text: And there’s something rather beautiful about the fact that the aṇu — the limited individual — is not abandoned.
blocks.directed: And there’s something rather beautiful about the fact that the aṇu — the limited individual — is not abandoned.

blocks.text: The journey begins from limitation.
blocks.directed: The journey begins from limitation.

blocks.text: But the destination is the recognition of freedom.
blocks.directed: But the destination is the recognition of freedom.

blocks.text: It’s not the replacement of the individual with a completely different metaphysical substance.
blocks.directed: It’s not the replacement of the individual with a completely different metaphysical substance.

blocks.text: It’s the disclosure of the universal nature underlying individuality.
blocks.directed: It’s the disclosure of the universal nature underlying individuality.

blocks.text: And now Vasugupta adds another sentence.
blocks.directed: And now Vasugupta adds another sentence.

blocks.text: A very short one.
blocks.directed: A very short one.

blocks.text: But an absolutely enormous claim.
blocks.directed: But an absolutely enormous claim.
